title: Ways to Make 5: Subitizing and Number Bonds
seo_title: Kindergarten Ways to make 5 Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Ways to make 5: perceptual subitizing (e.g., I see 5), conceptual subitizing (e.g., I see 4 and 1), using concrete materials to show ways to make 5
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on ways to make 5 for the BC curriculum: subitizing dot patterns, seeing parts, five frames, number bonds and stories. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: 5 can be made in many ways: 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 3 and 2, 4 and 1.
key_sub: Look for parts you know. I see 4 and 1, so I know there are 5.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Small groups can be seen at a glance without counting: I see 5.
  • You can also see the parts: I see 4 and 1, so there are 5.
  • 5 can be made in many ways: 0 and 5, 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 3 and 2, 4 and 1, 5 and 0.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Giving one part instead of the wholeAsk: How many in all? Put both parts together.
Counting one dot twiceLook for a pattern you know, like the 5 on a dot cube.
Thinking 2 and 2 make 5Count them: 1, 2, 3, 4. 2 and 3 make 5.

faq.a: Seeing how many are in a small group without counting. Perceptual subitizing is seeing 5 at once; conceptual subitizing is seeing parts, like 4 and 1, and knowing the total is 5.

faq.q: What are the ways to make 5?
faq.a: 0 and 5, 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 3 and 2, 4 and 1, and 5 and 0.

faq.q: How can I practise ways to make 5 at home?
faq.a: Hold up 5 fingers and fold some down, or hide some of 5 small toys under a cup and ask how many are hidden.

faq.q: Why learn ways to make 5 before 10?
faq.a: Five is a benchmark. Knowing its parts helps children see 6 as 5 and 1, and later make 10.
